1	"""Durable JSON-file persistence for the device store.
2	
3	The whole server state is kept in one versioned JSON document. A missing file
4	is created on first use; a corrupted file or a document whose version is not
5	understood makes the server refuse to start (state is never silently
6	discarded). Every change is written atomically: serialize to a temporary file
7	in the same directory, ``fsync`` it, take a hard-link backup of the current
8	target, ``os.replace`` it over the target, then ``fsync`` the parent
9	directory, so a crash never leaves a half-written or un-renamed state file.
10	
11	Persistence is transactional with respect to the in-memory store: the change
12	hook fires while the store lock is held (the mutation is visible but not yet
13	committed to callers). When the durable write succeeds it becomes the new
14	last-known-good state. When writing the temporary file, ``fsync`` or the
15	atomic replace fails (an :class:`OSError`), the previous last-known-good state
16	is restored into memory under the same lock and
17	:class:`PersistenceUnavailable` is raised so the HTTP layer answers
18	503/field=data_file; the failed mutation therefore never advances either
19	memory or the file.
20	
21	After the replace has landed, a failed directory fsync first rolls the rename
22	back: the pinned old inode is renamed over the target and a second directory
23	fsync flushes the rollback. When that rollback itself cannot be completed
24	durably — the rollback rename fails, or the second fsync fails — the failure
25	stays *decidable*: the old inode is kept under a ``.state-*.bak`` backup and
26	the new snapshot is taken off the formal path (parked under a
27	``.state-*.quarantine`` name the recovery scan never promotes, or deleted), so
28	the formal path is missing. The store is then marked degraded and reports 503
29	for the failed request.
30	
31	The degraded store also heals itself *within the same process*: the next
32	persist-able write runs, inside the storage lock, :meth:`JsonStateStore.heal`
33	before saving — the unique pinned ``.bak`` is fully verified (version=1,
34	commit generation, the complete-transaction sections, every cross-entity /
35	cursor / nonce / audit-chain semantic check, and exact equality with the
36	last committed in-memory state) and atomically promoted back onto the formal
37	path, same-transaction leftovers (``.quarantine``/``.tmp``) are removed, and
38	only then is that one triggering request committed (a single consecutive
39	``commit_seq`` advance). The request that originally got 503 is never
40	replayed; the healed commit carries only the later, current request. A
41	corrupt, dangling or ambiguous backup is refused promotion: the request gets
42	503/field=data_file, memory is rolled back, the formal path stays missing,
43	no leftover or generation moves, and the next write retries the heal. A
44	valid formal file always takes precedence over every backup. Restart
45	recovery remains the fallback that promotes the pinned backup.
46	
47	When even the decidable fallback cannot be achieved — the un-committed new
48	snapshot can be neither renamed aside nor deleted, so the formal path cannot be
49	proven missing — the store enters the *blocking state* (a sibling
50	``.state-*.block`` marker persists it across restarts). It never serves
51	that residual formal file as authoritative: every subsequent write is
52	503/field=data_file, in this process and after a restart, until the path is
53	vacated with exactly one verifiable backup (heal/restart then promote it and
54	clear the marker), or a file provably equal to the committed state is restored
55	onto the formal path (a valid formal always wins). Two or more
56	verifiable backups make promotion ambiguous and are likewise refused rather than picked by
57	name or mtime.
58	
59	A crash between steps can leave ``.state-*.tmp`` (staged document) or
60	``.state-*.bak`` (pinned previous inode) files beside the target. At the next
61	:func:`attach_persistence` these are resolved by
62	:func:`recover_crash_leftovers`: a valid formal file stays authoritative and
63	the leftovers are removed; with the formal file missing the highest
64	``commit_seq`` leftover that parses as version=1, carries the cursor and
65	``key_events`` sections (the footprint of one complete durable transaction),
66	and passes every semantic restore check is atomically recovered into place
67	(modification time newest-first breaks equal generations, and files without
68	the field keep the legacy newest-mtime rule); with none valid the leftovers
69	are removed and an empty state is created. An existing-but-corrupt formal
70	file still makes startup refuse rather than being silently overwritten.
71	
72	Every document carries a strictly-consecutive top-level ``commit_seq``: the
73	first empty state is written at 0 and each successful durable transaction
74	advances it exactly once (a failed write consumes no generation). A legacy
75	version=1 file without the field loads as generation 0; a present field must
76	be a non-negative integer or startup refuses (bool, negative, float and
77	string values are rejected) with the file untouched.
78	"""
79	from __future__ import annotations
80	
81	import copy
82	import errno
83	import json
84	import os
85	import sys
86	import tempfile
87	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
88	
89	from .storage import DeviceStore
90	
91	if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
92	    from .service import DeviceService
93	
94	#: Persistence format version understood by this build.
95	STATE_VERSION = 1
96	
97	#: Temporary-snapshot name parts, mirrored when scanning crash leftovers
98	#: (see :meth:`JsonStateStore.save`).
99	_TMP_PREFIX = ".state-"
100	_TMP_SUFFIX = ".tmp"
101	#: Suffix of the pre-replace hard-link backup pinning the previous inode.
102	_BAK_SUFFIX = ".bak"
103	#: Suffix of a new snapshot taken off the formal path when the rollback
104	#: itself cannot be completed durably. Such a file is deliberately *not* a
105	#: crash-recovery candidate (the scan only promotes ``.tmp``/``.bak``): the
106	#: transaction it staged was already reported failed and rolled back in
107	#: memory, so it must never be resurrected at the next startup.
108	_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX = ".quarantine"
109	#: Suffix of the durable marker left when a failed transaction could not be made
110	#: decidable: the formal path could not be vacated, so a possibly-un-committed
111	#: residual formal file sits beside a ``.bak`` of the last committed
112	#: inode. While such a marker exists the store is in the *blocking state*:
113	#: writes are refused (503/field=data_file) and the residual formal file is
114	#: never treated as authoritative, until an operator removes the marker (after resolving
115	#: the on-disk state) — or until heal finds the formal path missing with
116	#: exactly one verifiable backup, at which point it clears the marker itself.
117	_BLOCK_SUFFIX = ".block"
118	
119	#: Top-level commit-generation field. Every successful durable transaction
120	#: writes a document whose ``commit_seq`` is exactly one higher than the
121	#: previous one; the first (empty) state is created at 0. A legacy version-1
122	#: file written before this field loads as if it carried 0.
123	COMMIT_SEQ_KEY = "commit_seq"
124	
125	
126	def _valid_commit_seq(value: Any) -> bool:
127	    """A commit generation is a non-negative JSON integer (never a bool)."""
128	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0
129	
130	
131	def _commit_seq_of(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> int:
132	    """Rank a candidate by its commit generation; a missing/malformed one is 0.
133	
134	    Leftover snapshots are ranked leniently here (a leftover without the field
135	    predates commit generations and sorts at generation 0); the *formal*
136	    file's field is validated strictly by :meth:`JsonStateStore.load`.
137	    """
138	    value = document.get(COMMIT_SEQ_KEY, 0)
139	    return value if _valid_commit_seq(value) else 0
140	
141	
142	class StateFileError(Exception):
143	    """The state file is missing fields, corrupt, or has an unknown version."""
144	
145	
146	class PersistenceUnavailable(Exception):
147	    """A durable write failed; the transaction was rolled back in memory.
148	
149	    The in-memory store was restored to the last successfully persisted state
150	    under the store lock, the previous state file is intact, and the temporary
151	    file was removed. The HTTP layer reports this as 503/field=data_file.
152	    """
153	
154	
155	class JsonStateStore:
156	    """Versioned JSON document loaded from and atomically saved to one file."""
157	
158	    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
159	        self.path = path
160	        #: Commit generation the *next* save writes. The first (empty) state
161	        #: is created at 0; :func:`attach_persistence` re-seeds it from a
162	        #: loaded or recovered document (plus one) so generations stay
163	        #: strictly consecutive across restarts and recovery. It advances
164	        #: only once a save has completed durably, so a failed transaction
165	        #: never consumes a generation.
166	        self.commit_seq = 0
167	        #: Set once a transaction ends in the undecidable-on-disk state where
168	        #: the formal path is missing and the last committed inode survives
169	        #: only as a ``.bak`` (a failed rollback rename, or a rollback rename
170	        #: whose follow-up fsync failed). While set, every write first runs
171	        #: :meth:`heal` under the store lock: the pinned backup is fully
172	        #: verified and atomically promoted back onto the formal path, the
173	        #: same-transaction leftovers are cleaned, and only then the
174	        #: triggering write itself is committed. A heal that cannot verify or
175	        #: promote the backup keeps the store degraded and the write fails
176	        #: with 503/field=data_file, retryable by the next write.
177	        self.degraded = False
178	        #: Set instead of :attr:`degraded` when the failed transaction cannot even be
179	        #: made *decidable*: the formal path could not be vacated, so a
180	        #: possibly-un-committed residual file still occupies it while the last
181	        #: committed inode survives only as a ``.bak``. This is the
182	        #: *blocking state*. :meth:`heal` refuses to serve that residual
183	        #: formal as authoritative and :meth:`save` refuses every write (the HTTP
184	        #: layer answers 503/field=data_file), until the on-disk state is
185	        #: provably decidable again (formal missing and exactly one verifiable backup),
186	        #: or an operator resolves it. A sibling ``.state-*.block`` marker
187	        #: makes the state survive a restart, which keeps refusing while the residual
188	        #: formal file is present or no unique backup can be promoted.
189	        self.blocked = False
190	
191	    def load(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
192	        """Load the document, or ``None`` when the file does not exist yet.
193	
194	        Raises :class:`StateFileError` if the file cannot be decoded as JSON,
195	        is not a JSON object, carries a missing/unknown ``version``, or has a
196	        ``commit_seq`` that is present but not a non-negative integer (a bool,
197	        negative number, float or string). A file without ``commit_seq`` is a
198	        legacy version-1 document and loads as generation 0.
199	        """
200	        try:
201	            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
202	                raw = handle.read()
203	        except FileNotFoundError:
204	            return None
205	        except OSError as error:
206	            raise StateFileError(f"cannot read state file {self.path}: {error}")
207	
208	        try:
209	            document = json.loads(raw)
210	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
211	            raise StateFileError(
212	                f"state file is not valid JSON: {self.path} ({error})")
213	
214	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
215	            raise StateFileError("state document must be a JSON object")
216	        version = document.get("version")
217	        if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool):
218	            raise StateFileError("state document is missing a numeric 'version'")
219	        if version != STATE_VERSION:
220	            raise StateFileError(
221	                f"unsupported state file version: {version} "
222	                f"(this server supports {STATE_VERSION})")
223	        if COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document:
224	            commit_seq = document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]
225	            if not _valid_commit_seq(commit_seq):
226	                raise StateFileError(
227	                    f"state document '{COMMIT_SEQ_KEY}' must be a "
228	                    f"non-negative integer")
229	        return document
230	
231	    def save(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
232	        """Atomically replace the file with *state* (version stamped).
233	
234	        Writes a sibling temporary file, fsyncs it, then ``os.replace`` and
235	        fsyncs the parent directory, so the rename itself is durable across
236	        a crash — the target is either the previous full document or the new
237	        full one, never a truncated mix.
238	
239	        Before the replace a hard link to the current target is taken in the
240	        same directory. If the replace itself succeeds but the following
241	        directory fsync fails, that link is renamed back over the target,
242	        restoring the previous document's exact bytes *and inode*, and the
243	        rollback is flushed with a second directory fsync; every other
244	        pre-replace failure simply removes the temporary file, leaving the
245	        target untouched.
246	
247	        When the rollback itself cannot be completed durably — the rollback
248	        rename fails, or the second directory fsync fails — the store falls
249	        back to a *decidable* crash state instead of risking an un-committed
250	        snapshot at the formal path: the last committed inode is kept under a
251	        ``.bak`` backup and the new snapshot is taken off the formal path
252	        (renamed aside to a ``.quarantine`` name the recovery scan never
253	        promotes, or deleted), so the formal path is missing and the next
254	        write self-heals via :meth:`heal` (or, after a restart,
255	        :func:`recover_crash_leftovers`). Any failure propagates the
256	        underlying :class:`OSError` to the caller.
257	        """
258	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
259	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
260	        if self.degraded or self.blocked:
261	            # The formal path is not safely authoritative: degraded means it is
262	            # missing with the last committed inode pinned only as a .bak (a
263	            # save here could not be rolled back — there is no target to
264	            # back up); blocked means an un-decidable residual may occupy it.
265	            # Either way the persistence hook must run self.heal() first and
266	            # only reach this point once the formal path is restored. Refuse
267	            # any save that bypassed the heal.
268	            state = "blocked" if self.blocked else "degraded"
269	            raise OSError(
270	                f"state store for {self.path} is {state}; heal() must "
271	                f"resolve the on-disk state before another save")
272	        document = {"version": STATE_VERSION, **state}
273	        # Stamp the commit generation this save is committing. The counter
274	        # advances only after the replace and directory fsync succeed, so a
275	        # failed transaction (rolled back below) consumes no generation and
276	        # the next retry rewrites the same one — generations on disk stay
277	        # strictly consecutive.
278	        seq = self.commit_seq
279	        document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY] = seq
280	        tmp_handle = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
281	            mode="w", encoding="utf-8", dir=directory, delete=False,
282	            prefix=".state-", suffix=".tmp")
283	        tmp_path = tmp_handle.name
284	        backup_path: Optional[str] = None
285	        replaced = False
286	        try:
287	            json.dump(document, tmp_handle, separators=(",", ":"),
288	                      ensure_ascii=False)
289	            tmp_handle.flush()
290	            os.fsync(tmp_handle.fileno())
291	            tmp_handle.close()
292	            # Pin the old inode before renaming over it. On the first save the
293	            # target does not exist yet, so there is no old state to preserve.
294	            backup_path = _hardlink_backup(directory, self.path)
295	            os.replace(tmp_path, self.path)
296	            replaced = True
297	            # The rename is only durable once the directory entry is flushed;
298	            # without this fsync a crash can leave the directory pointing at
299	            # the pre-rename entry even though the replacement landed.
300	            _fsync_directory(directory)
301	        except BaseException:
302	            tmp_handle.close()
303	            _remove_quietly(tmp_path)
304	            if replaced and backup_path is not None:
305	                # The replacement landed but the following directory fsync
306	                # failed. Restore the pinned old inode atomically first (the
307	                # rename itself also drops the new inode)...
308	                try:
309	                    os.replace(backup_path, self.path)
310	                except OSError:
311	                    # ...the rollback rename itself failed. The formal path
312	                    # still holds the un-committed new inode, which must never
313	                    # become authoritative: move it off the path (the old
314	                    # inode stays pinned in the .bak), so the next startup
315	                    # sees a missing formal file and recovers that backup.
316	                    _vacate_new_snapshot(directory, self.path)
317	                    # Keep the backup: it is now the only copy of the last
318	                    # committed inode, so it must not be cleaned up below.
319	                    backup_path = None
320	                    if os.path.exists(self.path):
321	                        # The new snapshot could not be taken off the formal
322	                        # path: its presence is un-decidable (it is not
323	                        # the committed inode, yet occupies the authoritative name).
324	                        # Enter the blocking state rather than ever serve it as
325	                        # authoritative: persist a marker so a restart keeps
326	                        # refusing until the path is missing with a unique backup.
327	                        _write_block_marker(directory)
328	                        self.blocked = True
329	                    else:
330	                        self.degraded = True
331	                else:
332	                    backup_path = None
333	                    try:
334	                        _fsync_directory(directory)
335	                    except OSError:
336	                        # The rollback rename restored the old inode but its
337	                        # durability could not be flushed: this step failed
338	                        # too, so the transaction is still failed, never
339	                        # committed. Re-pin the restored inode as a .bak and
340	                        # vacate the formal path again, leaving exactly the
341	                        # "formal missing + old-inode .bak" state startup
342	                        # recovery resolves. When the path could not be
343	                        # vacated the old inode is still authoritative at it
344	                        # (the safe outcome), so the store is not degraded.
345	                        if _repin_old_inode(directory, self.path):
346	                            self.degraded = True
347	            if backup_path is not None:
348	                _remove_quietly(backup_path)
349	            raise
350	        # Commit is durable; drop the pinned old inode (best effort — a
351	        # leftover backup is harmless and cleaned up at the next startup).
352	        if backup_path is not None:
353	            _remove_quietly(backup_path)
354	            try:
355	                _fsync_directory(directory)
356	            except OSError:
357	                pass
358	        # The generation advances exactly once per durable commit.
359	        self.commit_seq = seq + 1

361	    def heal(self, baseline: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
362	        """Self-heal the degraded formal path from the pinned ``.bak``.
363	
364	        Called under the store lock by the persistence hook at the start of
365	        the next persist-able write after an undecidable write failure. The
366	        pinned backup is verified in full — version=1, a valid commit
367	        generation exactly one below the next save's generation, the whole
368	        cross-entity/cursor/nonce/audit-chain semantic restore, and exact
369	        equality with the process's last committed in-memory state — before
370	        it is promoted. Promotion is a same-directory *hard link*: the backup
371	        name keeps pinning the inode until the formal directory entry is
372	        fsync-durable, so a crash at this instant leaves either a valid
373	        formal file or the still-present backup, never neither. Only then are
374	        the same-transaction leftovers (redundant backups, staged ``.tmp``
375	        snapshots and the un-committed ``.quarantine``) removed.
376	
377	        A later write commit still goes through the normal atomic
378	        :meth:`save`, so healing consumes no generation: the healed commit
379	        advances ``commit_seq`` exactly once and carries only that triggering
380	        request — the earlier request that got 503 is never replayed.
381	
382	        Raises :class:`OSError` (mapped to 503/field=data_file by the caller)
383	        when no verifiable backup exists, two or more verifiable candidates
384	        exist (promotion is refused outright — choosing by name or mtime is
385	        forbidden), or the promotion cannot be made durable; in every such
386	        case the formal path stays missing, no leftover and no generation
387	        moves, :attr:`degraded` (or :attr:`blocked`) stays set, and the next
388	        write retries this heal. A formal file that reappeared valid and matching
389	        always takes precedence over every backup — but only in the *degraded*
390	        state. In the *blocking* state a residual formal file is never served as
391	        authoritative: heal refuses while it occupies the path, and only leaves the
392	        blocking state once the path is missing with exactly one verifiable backup to
393	        promote (the durable ``.block`` marker is cleared at that point).
394	        """
395	        if not (self.degraded or self.blocked):
396	            return
397	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
398	        leftovers = _leftover_tmp_paths(directory, self.path)
399	        quarantined = _quarantined_paths(directory, self.path)
400	
401	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
402	            # The formal path can only reappear (or, while blocked, never
403	            # have been vacated) out of band. A *valid formal always
404	            # takes precedence* — and that also resolves the blocked state
405	            # safely: the blocked residual is the un-committed new snapshot,
406	            # stamped with the NEXT generation (commit_seq == self.commit_seq), so
407	            # it can never match the committed baseline; only a file exactly
408	            # equal to the last committed state (generation one below, restores
409	            # and equals baseline) wins. When it does, keep it, sweep
410	            # every leftover/marker and resume normal saves. Anything else is
411	            # left untouched and refused.
412	            formal = _read_version1_document(self.path)
413	            formal_is_committed = (
414	                formal is not None
415	                and (COMMIT_SEQ_KEY not in formal
416	                     or _valid_commit_seq(formal[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]))
417	                and _commit_seq_of(formal) == self.commit_seq - 1
418	                and _document_restores(formal)
419	                and _document_payload_equals(formal, baseline))
420	            if formal_is_committed:
421	                _sweep_leftovers(
422	                    directory,
423	                    leftovers + quarantined
424	                    + _block_marker_paths(directory, self.path))
425	                self.degraded = False
426	                self.blocked = False
427	                return
428	            if self.blocked:
429	                raise OSError(
430	                    f"cannot self-heal {self.path}: the store is blocked by "
431	                    f"an un-resolved, un-committed file on the formal path")
432	            raise OSError(
433	                f"cannot self-heal {self.path}: the formal file reappeared "
434	                f"in an unexpected state")
435	
436	        # Verify every leftover against this process's last committed state.
437	        # Equality with *baseline* is the anti-dangling gate in addition to
438	        # the full semantic restore: a staged new snapshot (the transaction
439	        # already reported 503 and rolled back in memory) parses and may even
440	        # restore, but it can never equal the committed baseline and is
441	        # therefore never eligible here; quarantine files are never even
442	        # considered.
443	        eligible: List[str] = []
444	        for candidate in leftovers:
445	            try:
446	                with open(candidate, "rb") as handle:
447	                    raw = handle.read()
448	            except OSError:
449	                continue
450	            try:
451	                document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
452	            except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
453	                continue
454	            if not isinstance(document, dict):
455	                continue
456	            version = document.get("version")
457	            if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
458	                    or version != STATE_VERSION:
459	                continue
460	            if COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document and not _valid_commit_seq(
461	                    document[COMMIT_SEQ_KEY]):
462	                continue
463	            # The backup must pin the immediately-previous generation (a
464	            # field-less legacy backup ranks at 0 with the counter at 1).
465	            if _commit_seq_of(document) != self.commit_seq - 1:
466	                continue
467	            if not _document_restores(document):
468	                continue
469	            if not _document_payload_equals(document, baseline):
470	                continue
471	            eligible.append(candidate)
472	
473	        if not eligible:
474	            raise OSError(
475	                f"cannot self-heal {self.path}: no verifiable pinned backup "
476	                f"of the last committed state")
477	        # Two or more verifiable candidates are ambiguous even when their
478	        # bytes are identical: the choice between pin names must never be made
479	        # by name or mtime (both are forgeable and neither encodes which pin
480	        # the crashed transaction actually committed). Refuse promotion and
481	        # leave everything — formal path, leftovers, memory and generation —
482	        # exactly as found, so an operator or a restart resolves the ambiguity;
483	        # the next write retries the heal.
484	        if len(eligible) > 1:
485	            raise OSError(
486	                f"cannot self-heal {self.path}: {len(eligible)} verifiable "
487	                f"pinned backups of the last committed state; refusing to "
488	                f"choose between candidates")
489	        chosen = eligible[0]
490	
491	        # Promote with a hard link, never a rename: the backup keeps pinning
492	        # the inode until the new formal directory entry is fsync-durable.
493	        linked = False
494	        try:
495	            os.link(chosen, self.path)
496	            linked = True
497	            _fsync_directory(directory)
498	        except OSError:
499	            if linked:
500	                # The entry may not be durable. Drop the name we just added —
501	                # the inode stays pinned under the backup name — and best
502	                # effort flush the removal, then hand the failure back.
503	                _remove_quietly(self.path)
504	                try:
505	                    _fsync_directory(directory)
506	                except OSError:
507	                    pass
508	            raise
509	
510	        # The formal path durably names the committed inode; every pinned
511	        # copy, staged snapshot and demoted (quarantined) new snapshot is now
512	        # stale garbage. Sweep failures are harmless: a valid formal file
513	        # always wins the leftover scan at every later startup.
514	        _sweep_leftovers(directory, leftovers + quarantined)
515	        self.degraded = False
516	        if self.blocked:
517	            # The path was vacated out-of-band and the unique verifiable
518	            # backup is now durably authoritative: the undecidable condition
519	            # is gone, so drop the durable block marker and resume service.
520	            _clear_block_markers(directory, self.path)
521	            self.blocked = False

524	def _directory_fsync_unsupported(error: OSError) -> bool:
525	    """Classify *error* as "this platform/filesystem cannot fsync a directory".
526	
527	    Some POSIX network or special filesystems reject ``fsync`` on a
528	    directory fd with ``EINVAL`` (others use ``ENOTSUP``/``EOPNOTSUPP``);
529	    on Windows a directory cannot be opened for this at all and the CRT
530	    fails with ``EACCES`` (older runtimes raise ``EISDIR``). None of these
531	    means the data write itself failed — the file fsync and the atomic
532	    rename already landed — so the directory flush is safely skipped
533	    instead of failing (and rolling back) the whole transaction. Genuine
534	    I/O errors (``EIO``, ``EBADF``, permission problems elsewhere, ...)
535	    still propagate.
536	    """
537	    unsupported = {errno.EINVAL, errno.ENOTSUP,
538	                   getattr(errno, "EOPNOTSUPP", None)}
539	    if error.errno in unsupported:
540	        return True
541	    if sys.platform == "win32" and error.errno in (errno.EACCES, errno.EISDIR):
542	        return True
543	    return False
544

546	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> bool:
547	    """Flush *directory*'s metadata so a recent rename survives a crash.
548	
549	    Returns ``True`` when the flush ran. When the platform or underlying
550	    filesystem cannot fsync directories, the capability is safely skipped
551	    (returns ``False``) without reporting a failure; every other
552	    :class:`OSError` propagates to the caller. On platforms without
553	    ``O_DIRECTORY`` the plain read-only open still works.
554	    """
555	    flags = os.O_RDONLY
556	    try:
557	        dir_fd = os.open(directory, flags)
558	    except OSError as error:
559	        if _directory_fsync_unsupported(error):
560	            return False
561	        raise
562	    try:
563	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
564	    except OSError as error:
565	        if _directory_fsync_unsupported(error):
566	            return False
567	        raise
568	    finally:
569	        os.close(dir_fd)
570	    return True

573	def _hardlink_backup(directory: str, target: str) -> Optional[str]:
574	    """Pin the current *target*'s inode via a same-directory hard link.
575	
576	    Returns the backup path, or ``None`` when *target* does not exist yet
577	    (first save: there is no old state to preserve). The link is created in
578	    the same directory so it is guaranteed to be on the same file system and
579	    the subsequent rollback ``os.replace`` is a pure metadata rename. Raises
580	    :class:`OSError` if the link cannot be made; the caller treats that like
581	    any pre-replace failure (the target is still untouched).
582	    """
583	    if not os.path.exists(target):
584	        return None
585	    fd, backup = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
586	                                  suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
587	    os.close(fd)
588	    try:
589	        # mkstemp created an empty file under that unique name; remove it so
590	        # the name is free for the hard link.
591	        os.unlink(backup)
592	        os.link(target, backup)
593	    except OSError:
594	        _remove_quietly(backup)
595	        raise
596	    return backup
597

599	def _quarantine_path(directory: str) -> str:
600	    """Reserve a unique same-directory name for a demoted new snapshot."""
601	    fd, quarantine = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
602	                                      suffix=_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX)
603	    os.close(fd)
604	    # The empty placeholder only reserves the unique name; free it for the
605	    # rename that moves the new snapshot aside.
606	    os.unlink(quarantine)
607	    return quarantine

610	def _vacate_new_snapshot(directory: str, target: str) -> None:
611	    """Take the un-committed new snapshot off the formal path.
612	
613	    Used when a post-replace failure cannot be rolled back durably: the new
614	    inode must never become authoritative, so it is renamed aside to a
615	    ``.quarantine`` name (which the crash-leftover scan never promotes), and
616	    if even that rename is impossible it is deleted. Either way the formal
617	    path is missing afterwards; a pinned ``.bak`` of the last committed
618	    inode is the recovery candidate the next startup promotes. Best effort
619	    only — a failure here is swallowed because the caller still reports the
620	    transaction as failed and the old inode stays pinned elsewhere.
621	    """
622	    try:
623	        quarantine = _quarantine_path(directory)
624	        try:
625	            os.replace(target, quarantine)
626	        except OSError:
627	            _remove_quietly(quarantine)
628	            raise
629	    except OSError:
630	        _remove_quietly(target)

633	def _repin_old_inode(directory: str, target: str) -> bool:
634	    """Re-pin the restored old inode as a ``.bak`` and vacate *target*.
635	
636	    The rollback rename restored the last committed inode at *target*, but
637	    flushing that rollback failed, so it cannot be treated as durable. Pin
638	    the inode under a fresh backup name, then drop *target* (a second hard
639	    link to the same inode, so the unlink loses nothing), recreating the
640	    same "formal missing + old-inode .bak" triage a plain rollback failure
641	    leaves. Returns ``True`` when the formal path was vacated. If the inode
642	    cannot be pinned a second time it simply stays on the formal path — the
643	    last good state — and the function returns ``False`` so the caller does
644	    not mark the store degraded while a good file is authoritative.
645	    """
646	    try:
647	        fd, backup = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
648	                                      suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
649	        os.close(fd)
650	        os.unlink(backup)
651	        os.link(target, backup)
652	    except OSError:
653	        _remove_quietly(backup)
654	        # A second hard link cannot be made; instead rename the restored
655	        # target itself to the backup name — one atomic rename both keeps
656	        # the old inode (under the .bak) and vacates the formal path.
657	        try:
658	            fd, backup = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=_TMP_PREFIX,
659	                                          suffix=_BAK_SUFFIX)
660	            os.close(fd)
661	            os.unlink(backup)
662	            os.replace(target, backup)
663	        except OSError:
664	            _remove_quietly(backup)
665	            return False
666	    else:
667	        # target and backup now name the same restored inode; dropping
668	        # target leaves the inode pinned exactly once, under the backup name.
669	        _remove_quietly(target)
670	    return not os.path.exists(target)

673	def _read_version1_document(path: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
674	    """Parse *path* as a version-1 state document, or ``None`` if absent.
675	
676	    Mirrors :meth:`JsonStateStore.load` for arbitrary candidate paths (crash
677	    leftovers rather than the formal file): JSON object carrying
678	    ``version == 1`` or missing/unknown, returns the raw document or ``None``
679	    for a missing/unreadable/undecodable/wrong-version candidate.
680	    """
681	    try:
682	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
683	            raw = handle.read()
684	    except OSError:
685	        return None
686	    try:
687	        document = json.loads(raw)
688	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
689	        return None
690	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
691	        return None
692	    version = document.get("version")
693	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
694	            or version != STATE_VERSION:
695	        return None
696	    return document

699	def _candidate_is_section_complete(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
700	    """Require the durable-transaction sections a real snapshot always has.
701	
702	    Every snapshot produced by :meth:`JsonStateStore.save` is one full
703	    transaction and therefore carries the per-device sync cursor sections
704	    (``group_sync_cursors`` and ``message_sync_cursors``) and the
705	    ``key_events`` audit-chain section, each as a list — an empty list when
706	    the section has no records, but never absent. A leftover that parses and
707	    restores yet omits one of these sections is a partial/legacy document,
708	    not a crashed atomic commit: recovering it could silently drop a device's
709	    resume cursor or its audit chain, so it is not a valid crash-recovery
710	    candidate (a section-less *formal* file is still loaded leniently on the
711	    normal path; this gate applies only to leftover-snapshot recovery).
712	    """
713	    return all(isinstance(document.get(name), list)
714	               for name in ("group_sync_cursors", "message_sync_cursors",
715	                            "key_events"))

718	def _document_restores(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
719	    """Full semantic verification against :meth:`DeviceStore.restore_state`.
720	
721	    A structurally valid version-1 document is only a recovery candidate when
722	    a fresh store accepts its payload — the same group-session references,
723	    sequence continuity, nonce-set, per-device cursor range and ``updated_at``
724	    checks applied to the formal file.
725	    """
726	    try:
727	        DeviceStore().restore_state(
728	            {key: value for key, value in document.items()
729	             if key != "version"})
730	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
731	        return False
732	    return True

735	def _document_payload_equals(document: Dict[str, Any],
736	                             baseline: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
737	    """Compare a document's payload with the process's last committed state.
738	
739	    The on-disk document wraps the store snapshot with ``version`` and
740	    ``commit_seq``; strip those envelope fields and compare the remainder,
741	    semantically, to *baseline* (a value straight from
742	    :meth:`DeviceStore.snapshot_state`). Comparison goes through a fresh
743	    :meth:`DeviceStore.restore_state` + :meth:`DeviceStore.snapshot_state`
744	    round-trip rather than a raw dict diff, so an older *committed* document
745	    that legitimately predates an optional section (``used_nonces``, the
746	    sync-cursor sections, ``key_events`` ...) still matches a baseline whose
747	    snapshot fills those with their defaults — while a newer, un-committed
748	    snapshot cannot, because its extra business state (a revoked device, an
749	    appended message) round-trips to a different snapshot. This is the
750	    anti-dangling gate for self-heal: verifiable but newer content is never
751	    promoted. Returns ``False`` for any document that does not restore.
752	    """
753	    payload = {key: value for key, value in document.items()
754	               if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY)}
755	    try:
756	        candidate_store = DeviceStore()
757	        candidate_store.restore_state(payload)
758	        restored = candidate_store.snapshot_state()
759	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
760	        return False
761	    return restored == baseline
762

764	def _documents_payload_equal(left: Dict[str, Any],
765	                      right: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
766	    """Semantically compare two version-1 state documents' business payloads.
767	
768	    Envelope fields (``version``, ``commit_seq``) are ignored, so two
769	    copies of the same committed generation compare equal regardless of byte
770	    formatting, while a newer un-committed snapshot round-trips to a
771	    different snapshot. Returns ``False`` if either document fails to restore.
772	    """
773	    def _snapshot(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
774	        payload = {key: value for key, value in document.items()
775	                   if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY)}
776	        try:
777	            store = DeviceStore()
778	            store.restore_state(payload)
779	            return store.snapshot_state()
780	        except (ValueError, TypeError):
781	            return None
782	
783	    snap_left = _snapshot(left)
784	    snap_right = _snapshot(right)
785	    if snap_left is None or snap_right is None:
786	        return False
787	    return snap_left == snap_right

790	def _sweep_leftovers(directory: str, paths: List[str]) -> None:

956	      normal load then refuses startup, so present state is never silently

1054	    if os.path.exists(state_store.path):

1056	        # leftovers (including demoted snapshots parked in quarantine) are
1057	        # stale; an invalid one (including a present but malformed
1058	        # commit_seq) makes the normal load refuse startup, so neither the

1120	    for path in quarantined:

1125	    """Load *path* into *service* and persist every subsequent change.
1126	
1127	    A missing file is created immediately (with an empty version-1 document).
1128	    A corrupt or wrong-version file raises :class:`StateFileError` before the
1129	    server starts; the in-memory store is never touched in that case. After
1130	    attachment, each committed mutation rewrites the file atomically inside
1131	    the same store-lock transaction. A write/fsync/replace failure rolls the
1132	    in-memory store back to the last persisted state and raises
1133	    :class:`PersistenceUnavailable`; neither memory nor the file advances.
1134	    """
1135	    state_store = JsonStateStore(path)
1136	    # First resolve any temporary snapshot a crashed previous process left in
1137	    # the same directory: a valid formal file stays and leftovers are removed;
1138	    # a missing formal file is atomically restored from the newest verifiable
1139	    # version-1 leftover; with no valid candidate the leftovers are removed and
1140	    # the missing-file branch below creates an empty state.
1141	    try:
1142	        recover_crash_leftovers(state_store)
1143	    except OSError as error:
1144	        raise StateFileError(
1145	            f"cannot recover state file {path} from a crash leftover: "
1146	            f"{error}") from None

1148	    if document is None:
1149	        try:
1150	            state_store.save(service.store.snapshot_state())
1151	        except OSError as error:
1152	            raise StateFileError(
1153	                f"cannot create state file {path}: {error}") from None

1155	        # Resume commit generations exactly where the durable document left
1156	        # off (a legacy file without the field is generation 0): the next
1157	        # successful transaction writes commit_seq + 1, never repeating or
1158	        # skipping a generation after restart or crash recovery.
1159	        state_store.commit_seq = _commit_seq_of(document) + 1

1161	            service.store.restore_state(
1162	                {key: value for key, value in document.items()
1163	                 if key != "version"})
1164	        except (ValueError, TypeError) as error:
1165	            raise StateFileError(
1166	                f"state file has a malformed payload: {error}") from None

1168	    # Canonical deep copy of the last durably-committed state. It is only ever
1169	    # replaced with a snapshot whose save() succeeded, so it stays valid input
1170	    # for restore_state().
